turns.user: Can I buy a paper 30-minute ticket from a machine?
turns.agent:
No—the 30-minute ticket in the snapshot is a mobile ticket, with no paper equivalent, and it requires an internet-connected phone. So you can’t buy that product as a paper ticket from a machine. The 5 November 2026 snapshot lists an ordinary single ticket at 500 HUF and a block of ten at 4,500 HUF; those are separate products, not paper versions of the 30-minute ticket. For transfers on covered lines, the mobile 30-minute ticket allows transfers within its time window; if your final transfer happens before the window ends, you may finish that last ride after it expires.

Sources: BKK 30-minute ticket · BKK prices. This is snapshot-based guidance, not live verification; check BKK for current information.

turns.user: My phone has no mobile data and I won't have internet on the trip. What should I do?
turns.agent:
If you won’t have an internet-connected phone during the trip, don’t rely on the mobile 30-minute ticket; the snapshot says it requires internet access and has no paper equivalent. For a simple one-way ride, consider an ordinary single ticket instead (500 HUF in the 5 November 2026 snapshot). If you expect multiple rides or transfers, the right paper option depends on your route and how often you’ll travel; ordinary singles generally don’t cover voluntary transfers between street-level services. BKK ordinary single-ticket rules · BKK prices.

You could also arrange internet access before traveling if you specifically want to use the mobile ticket. I can help compare paper-friendly options if you tell me how many rides you expect and whether you’ll transfer between lines.
